dict.string: GeoDiscovery uses your camera to take photos and record videos. Each one is stamped with your GPS coordinates, address, and timestamp, so you always know exactly where and when it was taken. The camera is only accessed when you open a camera screen.
GeoDiscovery needs access to your microphone to record audio with your GPS-stamped videos.

GeoDiscovery uses your location while the app is open to stamp accurate GPS coordinates and a readable address onto your photos and videos. Your location is never tracked in the background. It leaves your device only when you choose to share it: sending your location to a friend, or sharing a photo or video, uploads those coordinates so your friends can see them on the map.

GeoDiscovery saves GPS-stamped photos and videos to your photo library so you can view them in the Photos app and share them with others.
GeoDiscovery reads your photo library so you can pick a profile picture. Photos you choose or capture are uploaded to our media host only when you share them with your friends.
